question: An engineer edits .claude/settings.json mid-session to add a new entry under permissions.allow for a Bash pattern the team just approved, then separately edits the model field in the same file to pin a different Claude version. Without restarting Claude Code, what should the engineer expect?
options: A) The model change takes effect immediately, but the permission entry requires the engineer to run /config manually before it is recognized
B) The new permission entry takes effect immediately through hot reloading, but the model change requires a restart before it applies
C) Neither change takes effect until restart, since settings files are only read once at process startup and never re-read afterward
D) Both changes take effect immediately, since Claude Code watches all settings files and hot-reloads every key without requiring a restart
correct_answers: B) The new permission entry takes effect immediately through hot reloading, but the model change requires a restart before it applies
explanations: Incorrect. model is one of the keys that does not hot-reload, and no manual /config step is documented as a workaround for the permission entry, which reloads on its own.

Correct. Claude Code watches settings files and hot-reloads most keys, including permissions, hooks, and env, without a restart, but model and outputStyle are documented exceptions that require a restart before the new value is used.
Incorrect. Claude Code does actively watch settings files during a session and hot-reloads most keys, so treating the file as read-once at startup is incorrect for keys like permissions.
Incorrect. Not every key hot-reloads; model is explicitly excluded from live reloading and only takes effect after a restart, so this overstates what applies immediately.
